from itertools import permutations

# Nationalities listed in room order (room 1..4 when used as tuples).
NAT = ["South Korea", "France", "Britain", "Germany"]

# Languages each person can speak, from the statements.
# German speaks all four countries' languages: Korean, French, English, German.
LANG = {
    "South Korea": {"Korean"},
    "France": {"French", "German"},
    "Britain": {"Korean", "English"},
    "Germany": {"Korean", "French", "English", "German"},
}

K, F, B, G = "South Korea", "France", "Britain", "Germany"


def comm(a, b):
    """Two people can communicate if they share at least one language."""
    return bool(LANG[a] & LANG[b])


def clauses(arr):
    """arr[i] is the nationality in room i+1. Neighbors are adjacent rooms."""
    pos = {n: i for i, n in enumerate(arr)}

    def nb(n):
        i = pos[n]
        return [arr[j] for j in (i - 1, i + 1) if 0 <= j < 4]

    k = pos[K] + 1
    g = pos[G] + 1
    return {
        "Korean room > German room": k > g,
        "Korean speaks no foreign language": LANG[K] == {"Korean"},
        "Korean communicates with no neighbor": not any(comm(K, x) for x in nb(K)),
        "French speaks German": "German" in LANG[F],
        "French communicates with no neighbor": not any(comm(F, x) for x in nb(F)),
        "British speaks Korean": "Korean" in LANG[B],
        "British communicates with exactly one neighbor": sum(comm(B, x) for x in nb(B)) == 1,
        "German speaks all four languages": {"Korean", "French", "English", "German"} <= LANG[G],
    }


# Exhaustive enumeration of all 4! arrangements.
all_perms = list(permutations(NAT))
solutions = [p for p in all_perms if all(clauses(p).values())]

print("Arrangements checked:", len(all_perms))
print("Consistent arrangements (room1..room4):")
for s in solutions:
    print("  ", s)

options = {
    "A": ("Britain", "Germany", "South Korea", "France"),
    "B": ("France", "Britain", "Germany", "South Korea"),
    "C": ("Germany", "Britain", "France", "South Korea"),
    "D": ("Germany", "Britain", "South Korea", "France"),
}

for letter, opt in options.items():
    print(f"Option {letter} {opt}: {'consistent' if opt in solutions else 'inconsistent'}")

# Submitted answer is D. Show which clauses fail for it.
submitted = options["D"]
print("Clause results for submitted answer D:")
for name, val in clauses(submitted).items():
    print(f"  {name}: {val}")

if submitted in solutions:
    print("CHECK PASS")
else:
    print("CHECK FAIL")

# Exhaustive, so the unique solution is settled by enumeration.
if len(solutions) == 1:
    ans = [L for L, o in options.items() if o == solutions[0]]
    print("Unique consistent answer option:", ans[0] if ans else "not among options")
